newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai residents switch to current accounts.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai residents switch to current accounts.

text.p: Following two interest rate cuts this year, Shanghai residents are putting more of their bank deposits into current accounts instead of fixed-term deposits, the Liberation Daily reported on Sunday.

At the end of September, total individual bank deposits in Shanghai reached 178.707 billion yuan, an increase of 38.974 billion over the end of 1995 and an increase of 2.266 billion over the end of June, it said.
Of this increase, more money went into current accounts than fixed-term deposits, showing that individuals wanted to have the money available to invest in the stock and bond markets, it said.
In the first nine months of 1996, total securities turnover on the Shanghai Stock Exchange was 1.6 trillion yuan, a 310 percent increase over the same 1995 period, it said.

Of this figure, trading in treasury bonds was 1.06 trillion yuan, a 710 percent increase over the same 1995 period, much of it a result of open-market operations started by the central bank this year, it said. It gave no further details.
